blocked.title: Control depth cannot be made tenant-causal in Cohort 1 without changing rottay and evnto.
blocked.advisorRuling: Fable ruled option (a): delete the engine-tier --ds-button-{variant}-shadow defaults so the role floor shows through, on the stated premise that rottay/evnto 'AUTHOR their chrome shadows, chrome stays senior, so their computed values are untouched'. It attached one verification: census those artifacts for full 10-variant shadow coverage.

censusRun.method: grep of --ds-button-{variant}-shadow declarations in each shipped vertical artifact
censusRun.verdict: THE PREMISE IS FALSE. No vertical authors more than the primary variant.

blocked.consequence: Deleting the engine defaults flattens SIX variants in ALL THREE verticals, including rottay and evnto which are outside this round. That is not a declared delta on an unauthored variant; it is a visual change to two products this cohort has no mandate to touch.
blocked.whyTheAlternativesAlsoFail: Rebasing the engine default onto the role channel does not help either, and for a mechanical reason: --ds-material-control-shadow and all three of its state channels are DECLARED on :root as `none`, so any var() chain that reaches them resolves to none rather than falling through. Role-senior and role-as-fallback both flatten. The pattern that worked six times elsewhere in this cohort (rebase the default onto a tenant-reachable authority) works precisely because those authorities were NOT :root-declared.
blocked.proposal: Two admissible routes, both needing adjudication because both reach outside Cohort 1: (1) change the :root default of --ds-material-control-shadow so it is not a hard `none`, which is a foundation change affecting every consumer; or (2) have each vertical AUTHOR its control shadow posture before the engine defaults are deleted, which is a rottay/evnto work item. Claude did not pick one: either would change verticals this round does not own.
blocked.disposition: BLOCKED pending adjudication. No edit was made.

probeBuiltAndProven.coverage: 72 cells per vertical — 12 variants x 4 states (rest/hover/active/selected) x 2 colour modes, for rottay, evnto and bithire
probeBuiltAndProven.comparisonRule: Reference strings compared verbatim; terminal --ds-shadow-* values deliberately NOT resolved, because the pins are by reference and those tokens are dark-aware. Resolving them would fail on a legitimate dark-mode difference and would test the wrong property.
probeBuiltAndProven.negativeDrill: Simulating the naive deletion by flipping three engine-resolved cells to the role floor produces 3 regressions and the verdict "the deletion is NOT safe as sequenced". An unchanged snapshot returns PRESERVED. The probe is therefore not fail-open.
probeBuiltAndProven.pathTrapFound: The mapping INVERTS between the two halves: the theme source for rottay is brand-themes/platform/ while its artifact is artifacts/rottay/. The first probe run failed on exactly this. Any code touching both halves must carry both keys.

supersededBy.advisorClaimRefutedOnSecondPass: The advisor warned that deleting an engine --ds-button-ghost-shadow-hover: none would flip ghost hover to a soft shadow. Measured false: ghost, dashed, text and link declare hover and active as a SELF-REFERENCE to their own rest value, not none. Zero flip hazards across all variants, so those four need no state pins and the pin list is smaller than specified. The census also found the ai variant carrying a real value, which the advisor six-variant list omitted — eight rest pins are required, not six.
supersededBy.readyForExecution: The sequence is now fully specified by evidence rather than by prose: pin the eight rests BY REFERENCE in brand-themes/platform and brand-themes/evnto, pin the non-self-referencing states in each _source/extension.css, regenerate with build:vertical-css, add the skin role fallbacks, then delete the engine declarations — running the probe between steps and requiring PRESERVED before the deletion lands.
